references.text: The daily burnt offering with one lamb in the morning and one in the evening is first described in Exodus, and Numbers 28:4 repeats this instruction.
Describes the second lamb to be offered in the evening, parallel to 'bein ha'arbayim' (between the evenings) in Numbers 28:4.
Elijah sacrificed at the time of the evening offering, referring to the daily sacrificial practice described in Numbers 28:4.
Reference to the time when the grain offering was presented, linked to the daily evening offering.
Daniel received the vision at the time of the evening offering, connecting it to the daily sacrifice described in Numbers 28:4.
Ezekiel's vision of the future temple includes daily burnt offerings with a lamb in the morning, reflecting the instructions in Numbers 28:4.
John the Baptist calls Jesus 'the Lamb of God', which has a thematic connection to the sacrificial lamb in the daily burnt offering.
Peter describes Christ as a lamb without blemish or spot, fulfilling the type of the daily sacrificial lamb.
